greek: Αὗται δὲ αἱ γενέσεις τῶν υἱῶν Νωε, Σημ, Χαμ, Ιαφεθ, καὶ ἐγενήθησαν αὐτοῖς υἱοὶ μετὰ τὸν κατακλυσμόν.
hint: The origins of the sons of Noah: the Table of Nations begins.

notes.text: The word of 2:4, 5:1 and 6:9, for the Hebrew *tôlĕdōt*.
Glossed again, first in this chapter.

reading: [[these|these, the nearer, what follows]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand]], [[the origins|the origins, the sources, the productive causes, the beginnings, the manners of birth, the races and descents, the productions and generations, the creations and the created things]] of the sons of [[name:Νωε]], [[name:Σημ]], [[name:Χαμ]], [[name:Ιαφεθ]], and [[came into being|came to be, arose, were brought into existence]] to them sons [[into the middle of|into the middle of, coming among, in pursuit and quest of, after]] [[the deluge|the deluge, the inundation]].

names.gloss: (Νωε, from Hebrew Nōaḥ, usually connected with nûaḥ, "to rest")
(Σημ, from Hebrew Šēm, "name")
(Χαμ, from Hebrew Ḥām, usually connected with ḥam, "hot")
(Ιαφεθ, from Hebrew Yepet, which 9:27 ties to pātâ, "to make wide")

greek: Υἱοὶ Ιαφεθ· Γαμερ καὶ Μαγωγ καὶ Μαδαι καὶ Ιωυαν καὶ Ελισα καὶ Θοβελ καὶ Μοσοχ καὶ Θιρας.
hint: The sons of Japheth.

notes.text: [[flag]] Not in the Hebrew, whose sons of Japheth are seven: Gomer, Magog, Madai, Javan, Tubal, Meshech and Tiras. The Greek adds Ελισα, the son of Javan in 10:4.
The name of Revelation 20:8, τὸν Γὼγ καὶ Μαγώγ.
The form 4:22 gave Tubal-cain; here Hebrew *Tûbal*.

reading: Sons of [[name:Ιαφεθ]]; [[name:Γαμερ]] and [[name:Μαγωγ]] and [[name:Μαδαι]] and [[name:Ιωυαν]] and [[name:Ελισα]] and [[name:Θοβελ]] and [[name:Μοσοχ]] and [[name:Θιρας]].

names.gloss: (Γαμερ, from Hebrew Gōmer, of uncertain meaning)
(Μαγωγ, from Hebrew Māgôg, of uncertain meaning)
(Μαδαι, from Hebrew Māday, the Medes)
(Ιωυαν, from Hebrew Yāwān, Ionia, the Greeks)
(Ελισα, from Hebrew ʾĔlîšâ, of uncertain meaning)
(Θοβελ, from Hebrew Tûbal, of uncertain meaning)
(Μοσοχ, from Hebrew Mešek, of uncertain meaning)
(Θιρας, from Hebrew Tîrās, of uncertain meaning)

greek: καὶ υἱοὶ Γαμερ· Ασχαναζ καὶ Ριφαθ καὶ Θοργαμα.
hint: The sons of Gomer.

notes.text: [[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus alone reads Θεργαμα.

reading: and sons of [[name:Γαμερ]]; [[name:Ασχαναζ]] and [[name:Ριφαθ]] and [[name:Θοργαμα]].

names.gloss: (Ασχαναζ, from Hebrew ʾAškĕnaz, of uncertain meaning)
(Ριφαθ, from Hebrew Rîpat, of uncertain meaning)
(Θοργαμα, from Hebrew Tōgarmâ, of uncertain meaning)

greek: καὶ υἱοὶ Ιωυαν· Ελισα καὶ Θαρσις, Κίτιοι, Ῥόδιοι.
hint: The sons of Javan, two of them named as Greek peoples.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew has two names, *Kittîm* and *Dōdānîm*. The Greek has two peoples: the Citians of Kition in Cyprus, and the Rhodians, as if reading *Rōdānîm*, the spelling of 1 Chronicles 1:7.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus reads Κήτιοι.

reading: and sons of [[name:Ιωυαν]]; [[name:Ελισα]] and [[name:Θαρσις]], [[name:Κίτιοι]], [[name:Ῥόδιοι]].

names.gloss: (Θαρσις, from Hebrew Taršîš, of uncertain meaning)
(Κίτιοι, the people of Kition in Cyprus; Hebrew Kittîm)
(Ῥόδιοι, the people of Rhodes; Hebrew Dōdānîm)

greek: ἐκ τούτων ἀφωρίσθησαν νῆσοι τῶν ἐθνῶν ἐν τῇ γῇ αὐτῶν, ἕκαστος κατὰ γλῶσσαν ἐν ταῖς φυλαῖς αὐτῶν καὶ ἐν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν αὐτῶν.
hint: The islands of the nations are marked off, each by its tongue.

notes.text: ἀφορίζω, the verb of the river parting at 2:10; the Hebrew *nipredû* is the verb of 2:10 too, *pārad*.
νῆσος, *an island*, one sense, is plain text; the Hebrew *ʾiyyê* is *coastlands*.
Middle Liddell's first sense is *a number of people accustomed to live together*; *a nation* is the second, and *the nations, Gentiles* the New Testament's.

reading: [[out of|out of, forth from, from]] [[of these|of these, of the nearer, of what follows]] [[were marked off by boundaries|were marked off by boundaries, were marked off for themselves, were distinguished and determined and defined, were set apart and separated]] islands [[of the numbers of people accustomed to live together|of the numbers of people accustomed to live together, of the companies and bodies of men, of the hosts, of the swarms and flocks, of the nations and peoples, of the nations and gentiles, of the special classes, of the castes and tribes, of the sexes]] [[in the earth|within, inside of, and by means of the land, the dry ground, the terrestrial realm]] of them, [[every|every, every one, each, each one, all and each one, singly and by itself, each by himself]] [[down|down, downwards, down from, down upon, over, upon]] [[tongue|tongue, tongue as the organ of speech, tongue and language, mouthpiece of a pipe]] [[in the races|within, inside of, and by means of the races, the tribes, the bodies united by ties of blood and descent, the clans, the tribes by local habitation, the hundreds and counties, the contingents furnished by a tribe, the brigades]] of them and [[in the numbers of people accustomed to live together|within, inside of, and by means of the numbers of people accustomed to live together, the companies and bodies of men, the hosts, the swarms and flocks, the nations and peoples, the nations and gentiles, the special classes, the castes and tribes, the sexes]] of them.

greek: Υἱοὶ δὲ Χαμ· Χους καὶ Μεσραιμ, Φουδ καὶ Χανααν.
hint: The sons of Ham.

notes.text: The Hebrew *Kûš*, which 2:13 rendered Αἰθιοπία.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus reads Μεσραιν, here and at 10:13.

reading: Sons [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand]], of [[name:Χαμ]]; [[name:Χους]] and [[name:Μεσραιμ]], [[name:Φουδ]] and [[name:Χανααν]].

names.gloss: (Χους, from Hebrew Kûš, the land 2:13 calls Αἰθιοπία)
(Μεσραιμ, from Hebrew Miṣrayim, Egypt)
(Φουδ, from Hebrew Pûṭ, of uncertain meaning)
(Χανααν, from Hebrew Kĕnaʿan, of uncertain meaning)

greek: υἱοὶ δὲ Χους· Σαβα καὶ Ευιλα καὶ Σαβαθα καὶ Ρεγμα καὶ Σαβακαθα. υἱοὶ δὲ Ρεγμα· Σαβα καὶ Δαδαν.
hint: The sons of Cush and of Raamah.

notes.text: Two Hebrew names, *Sĕbāʾ* and *Šĕbāʾ*, printed alike in Greek, which has no letter for *š*. Both take the English form of the first.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus alone reads Ρεγχμα, both times.

reading: sons [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand]], of [[name:Χους]]; [[name:Σαβα]] and [[name:Ευιλα]] and [[name:Σαβαθα]] and [[name:Ρεγμα]] and [[name:Σαβακαθα]]. sons [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand]], of [[name:Ρεγμα]]; [[name:Σαβα]] and [[name:Δαδαν]].

names.gloss: (Σαβα, from Hebrew Sĕbāʾ; the second Σαβα of the verse is Hebrew Šĕbāʾ, Sheba)
(Ευιλα, from Hebrew Ḥăwîlâ, the name 2:11 gives as Ευιλατ, usually connected with ḥôl, "sand")
(Σαβαθα, from Hebrew Sabtâ, of uncertain meaning)
(Ρεγμα, from Hebrew Raʿmâ, of uncertain meaning)
(Σαβακαθα, from Hebrew Sabtĕkāʾ, of uncertain meaning)
(Δαδαν, from Hebrew Dĕdān, of uncertain meaning)

greek: Χους δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Νεβρωδ. οὗτος ἤρξατο εἶναι γίγας ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς·
hint: Nimrod, the first giant on the earth.

notes.text: The word of 6:4, for the Hebrew *gibbōr*, *mighty one*. Middle Liddell's first sense is *the Giants*, *the sons of Gaia*, and *mighty* is the adjective.

reading: [[name:Χους]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand]], [[begot|begot, engendered, brought forth, produced]] — one completed act seen whole, not a process observed in progress — [[name:Νεβρωδ]]. [[this|this, the nearer, what follows]] [[began|began, made a beginning, made a beginning of, began from]] to be [[giant|giant, son of Gaia, mighty]] [[upon|upon, on, in, at, near]] [[of the earth|of the land, of the dry ground, of the terrestrial realm]];

names.gloss: (Νεβρωδ, from Hebrew Nimrōd, usually connected with mārad, "to rebel")

greek: οὗτος ἦν γίγας κυνηγὸς ἐναντίον κυρίου τοῦ θεοῦ· διὰ τοῦτο ἐροῦσιν Ὡς Νεβρωδ γίγας κυνηγὸς ἐναντίον κυρίου.
hint: A giant hunter before the Lord God, and a saying about him.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *lipnê YHWH*, *before YHWH*; the Greek adds τοῦ θεοῦ, the first time in the verse and not the second.
Filed under the Doric and Attic κυναγός, *a hound-leader*, i.e. *a huntsman*; the Hebrew is *ṣayid*.
The imperfect in short, *was, and kept on being*: the full formula's *as* would stand beside ὡς's headword.
Capitalised because it opens a saying, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

reading: [[this|this, the nearer, what follows]] was, and kept on being, [[giant|giant, son of Gaia, mighty]] [[hound-leader|hound-leader, huntsman]] [[in the presence of|in the presence of, before, opposite and face to face, against]] [[of lord|of lord, of master, of the one having power and authority over]] [[of the God|of him who is God definitively, of the one the article marks out, of the known and the only]]; [[through|through, throughout and over, during, by aid of and by means of, by reason of, because of, for the sake of]] [[this|this, the nearer, what follows]] [[they will say|they will say, they will speak, they will declare, they will call by name, they will tell]] [[as|as, according as, considering, like]] [[name:Νεβρωδ]] [[giant|giant, son of Gaia, mighty]] [[hound-leader|hound-leader, huntsman]] [[in the presence of|in the presence of, before, opposite and face to face, against]] [[of lord|of lord, of master, of the one having power and authority over]].

greek: καὶ ἐγένετο ἀρχὴ τῆς βασιλείας αὐτοῦ Βαβυλὼν καὶ Ορεχ καὶ Αρχαδ καὶ Χαλαννη ἐν τῇ γῇ Σεννααρ.
hint: Babylon and the cities of Shinar.

notes.text: For the Hebrew *Bābel*: the Greek gives the city its Greek name, as it will not at 11:9.
The word of 1:1, and of the rivers' heads at 2:10.

reading: and [[came into being|came to be, arose, was brought into existence]] [[beginning|beginning, origin, first cause, headship and rule and governing precedence]] [[of the kingdom|of the kingdom, of the dominion, of the hereditary monarchy]] of him [[name:Βαβυλὼν]] and [[name:Ορεχ]] and [[name:Αρχαδ]] and [[name:Χαλαννη]] [[in the earth|within, inside of, and by means of the land, the dry ground, the terrestrial realm]] [[name:Σεννααρ]].

names.gloss: (Βαβυλών, the Greek name of Hebrew Bābel, which 11:9 ties to bālal, "to confuse")
(Ορεχ, from Hebrew ʾErek, the city Uruk)
(Αρχαδ, from Hebrew ʾAkkad, the city Akkad)
(Χαλαννη, from Hebrew Kalnēh, of uncertain meaning)
(Σεννααρ, from Hebrew Šinʿār, the plain of Babylonia)

greek: ἐκ τῆς γῆς ἐκείνης ἐξῆλθεν Ασσουρ καὶ ᾠκοδόμησεν τὴν Νινευη καὶ τὴν Ροωβωθ πόλιν καὶ τὴν Χαλαχ
hint: Asshur goes out and builds Nineveh.

notes.text: The Hebrew *yāṣāʾ ʾaššûr* can be read *Asshur went out* or *he went out to Assyria*. The Greek has no preposition, and Ασσουρ stands as the subject.
The Hebrew *Rĕḥōbōt ʿîr* joins *ʿîr*, *city*, to the name; the Greek translates it.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus alone reads Ροωβως; it also leaves out the last τήν, which the Berlin papyrus, 911, has.

reading: [[out of|out of, forth from, from]] [[of the earth|of the land, of the dry ground, of the terrestrial realm]] [[of that|of that, of the one there, of the more remote]] [[went out of|went out of, came out, went away and marched off, went forth]] [[name:Ασσουρ]] and [[built a house|built a house, built, built for himself]] [[name:Νινευη]] and [[name:Ροωβωθ]] [[the city|the city, the citadel, the country, the body of citizens, the state]] and [[name:Χαλαχ]]

names.gloss: (Ασσουρ, from Hebrew ʾAššûr, the name of Assyria, of its god and of its city)
(Νινευη, from Hebrew Nînĕwēh, the city Nineveh)
(Ροωβωθ, from Hebrew Rĕḥōbōt, "broad places")
(Χαλαχ, from Hebrew Kelaḥ, the city Kalhu)

greek: καὶ τὴν Δασεμ ἀνὰ μέσον Νινευη καὶ ἀνὰ μέσον Χαλαχ· αὕτη ἡ πόλις ἡ μεγάλη. —
hint: Resen, the great city.

notes.text: For the Hebrew *Resen*, with Δ for *R*.
Rahlfs prints a dash after the verse, closing a section.

reading: and [[name:Δασεμ]] [[up to middle|up to, up along, and throughout the middle, in the middle, the centre, mid, between two]] [[name:Νινευη]] and [[up to middle|up to, up along, and throughout the middle, in the middle, the centre, mid, between two]] [[name:Χαλαχ]]; [[this|this, the nearer, what follows]] [[the city|the city, the citadel, the country, the body of citizens, the state]] the [[big|big, great, tall, full-grown, vast and high, spacious and wide, strong and mighty, violent, loud, prevailing, weighty and important]].

names.gloss: (Δασεμ, from Hebrew Resen, of uncertain meaning)

greek: καὶ Μεσραιμ ἐγέννησεν τοὺς Λουδιιμ καὶ τοὺς Ενεμετιιμ καὶ τοὺς Λαβιιμ καὶ τοὺς Νεφθαλιιμ
hint: The peoples descended from Mizraim.

notes.text: Peoples, in the Hebrew plural *-îm*, which the Greek keeps as *-ιιμ* and does not decline.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus alone moves it to follow τοὺς Λουδιιμ.

reading: and [[name:Μεσραιμ]] [[begot|begot, engendered, brought forth, produced]] [[name:Λουδιιμ]] and [[name:Ενεμετιιμ]] and [[name:Λαβιιμ]] and [[name:Νεφθαλιιμ]]

names.gloss: (Λουδιιμ, the Hebrew plural Lûdîm)
(Ενεμετιιμ, the Hebrew plural ʿĂnāmîm)
(Λαβιιμ, the Hebrew plural Lĕhābîm)
(Νεφθαλιιμ, the Hebrew plural Naptuḥîm)

greek: καὶ τοὺς Πατροσωνιιμ καὶ τοὺς Χασλωνιιμ, ὅθεν ἐξῆλθεν ἐκεῖθεν Φυλιστιιμ, καὶ τοὺς Καφθοριιμ. —
hint: The Philistines come out from the Casluhim.

notes.text: Middle Liddell leaves its first gloss, *whence, from which*, untagged; the first it tags is *from whom*, which is the verse's sense.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus alone reads Χασμωνιειμ, and reads Χαφθοριιμ, where Καφθοριιμ is the Berlin papyrus's, 911.
Rahlfs prints a dash after the verse, closing a section.

reading: and [[name:Πατροσωνιιμ]] and [[name:Χασλωνιιμ]], [[from whom|from whom, from whatever source and in what manner soever, where, whence and wherefore]] [[went out of|went out of, came out, went away and marched off, went forth]] [[from that place|from that place, thence, thereafter, next]] [[name:Φυλιστιιμ]], and [[name:Καφθοριιμ]].

names.gloss: (Πατροσωνιιμ, the Hebrew plural Patrusîm, of Patrôs, Upper Egypt)
(Χασλωνιιμ, the Hebrew plural Kasluḥîm)
(Φυλιστιιμ, the Hebrew plural Pĕlištîm, the Philistines)
(Καφθοριιμ, the Hebrew plural Kaptōrîm, of Kaptôr, usually taken for Crete)

greek: Χανααν δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Σιδῶνα πρωτότοκον καὶ τὸν Χετταῖον
hint: Canaan's first-born, Sidon, and the Hittite.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *wĕʾet-ḥēt*, *and Heth*, a name. The Greek has the people, *the Hittite*, as the Hebrew has the peoples from the next verse on.
πρωτότοκος, *first-born*, one sense, is plain text, as at 4:4.

reading: [[name:Χανααν]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand]], [[begot|begot, engendered, brought forth, produced]] [[name:Σιδῶνα]] first-born and [[name:Χετταῖον]]

names.gloss: (Σιδών, from Hebrew Ṣîdōn, usually connected with ṣûd, "to hunt, to fish")
(Χετταῖος, for Hebrew Ḥēt, the name the Hebrew gives here, whose people are the Ḥittî, the Hittites)

greek: καὶ τὸν Ιεβουσαῖον καὶ τὸν Αμορραῖον καὶ τὸν Γεργεσαῖον
hint: The Jebusite, the Amorite, the Girgashite.

notes.text: The peoples are singular, with the article, as the Hebrew *hayĕbûsî*: each name stands for its people.

reading: and [[name:Ιεβουσαῖον]] and [[name:Αμορραῖον]] and [[name:Γεργεσαῖον]]

names.gloss: (Ιεβουσαῖος, from Hebrew Yĕbûsî, "of Jebus")
(Αμορραῖος, from Hebrew ʾĔmōrî, of uncertain meaning)
(Γεργεσαῖος, from Hebrew Girgāšî, of uncertain meaning)

greek: καὶ τὸν Ευαῖον καὶ τὸν Αρουκαῖον καὶ τὸν Ασενναῖον
hint: The Hivite, the Arkite, the Sinite.

notes.text: The Hebrew *ʿArqî* and *Sînî*, printed with an added vowel.

reading: and [[name:Ευαῖον]] and [[name:Αρουκαῖον]] and [[name:Ασενναῖον]]

names.gloss: (Ευαῖος, from Hebrew Ḥiwwî, of uncertain meaning)
(Αρουκαῖος, from Hebrew ʿArqî, "of Arqa")
(Ασενναῖος, from Hebrew Sînî, of uncertain meaning)

greek: καὶ τὸν Ἀράδιον καὶ τὸν Σαμαραῖον καὶ τὸν Αμαθι. καὶ μετὰ τοῦτο διεσπάρησαν αἱ φυλαὶ τῶν Χαναναίων,
hint: The Arvadite, the Zemarite, the Hamathite; then the Canaanites scatter.

notes.text: Rahlfs prints it with a breathing and an accent, as a Greek word: the man of Arados, the island city.

reading: and [[name:Ἀράδιον]] and [[name:Σαμαραῖον]] and [[name:Αμαθι]]. and [[into the middle of|into the middle of, coming among, in pursuit and quest of, after]] [[this|this, the nearer, what follows]] [[were scattered abroad|were scattered abroad, were thrown about, were squandered]] [[the races|the races, the tribes, the bodies united by ties of blood and descent, the clans, the tribes by local habitation, the hundreds and counties, the contingents furnished by a tribe, the brigades]] of [[name:Χαναναίων]],

names.gloss: (Ἀράδιος, the man of Arados, the island city; Hebrew ʾArwādî)
(Σαμαραῖος, from Hebrew Ṣĕmārî, "of Ṣumur")
(Αμαθι, from Hebrew Ḥămātî, "of Hamath")
(Χαναναῖος, from Hebrew Kĕnaʿănî, "of Canaan")

greek: καὶ ἐγένοντο τὰ ὅρια τῶν Χαναναίων ἀπὸ Σιδῶνος ἕως ἐλθεῖν εἰς Γεραρα καὶ Γάζαν, ἕως ἐλθεῖν Σοδομων καὶ Γομορρας, Αδαμα καὶ Σεβωιμ, ἕως Λασα. —
hint: The borders of the Canaanites, from Sidon to Gaza and to Lasha.

notes.text: *Until to come*: the Hebrew *bōʾăkâ*, *as you come*, rendered word for word with an infinitive.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus leaves out τῶν, reads ἕως before Σοδομων, and has Δασα for Λασα, where Λασα is the Berlin papyrus's, 911.
Rahlfs prints a dash after the verse, closing a section.

reading: and [[came into being|came to be, arose, were brought into existence]] [[the boundaries|the boundaries, the limits, the borders, the frontier]] of [[name:Χαναναίων]] [[from|from, away from, far from, apart from]] [[name:Σιδῶνος]] [[until|until, till, while, so long as]] [[to come|to come, to go, to go back and return, to be going to and intend, to come within a little of and be near]] [[into|into, to, in, rest in]] [[name:Γεραρα]] and [[name:Γάζαν]], [[until|until, till, while, so long as]] [[to come|to come, to go, to go back and return, to be going to and intend, to come within a little of and be near]] [[name:Σοδομων]] and [[name:Γομορρας]], [[name:Αδαμα]] and [[name:Σεβωιμ]], [[until|until, till, while, so long as]] [[name:Λασα]].

names.gloss: (Γεραρα, from Hebrew Gĕrār, of uncertain meaning)
(Γάζα, from Hebrew ʿAzzâ, "strong")
(Σόδομα, from Hebrew Sĕdōm, of uncertain meaning)
(Γόμορρα, from Hebrew ʿĂmōrâ, of uncertain meaning)
(Αδαμα, from Hebrew ʾAdmâ, of uncertain meaning)
(Σεβωιμ, from Hebrew Ṣĕbōyim, of uncertain meaning)
(Λασα, from Hebrew Lešaʿ, of uncertain meaning)

greek: οὗτοι υἱοὶ Χαμ ἐν ταῖς φυλαῖς αὐτῶν κατὰ γλώσσας αὐτῶν ἐν ταῖς χώραις αὐτῶν καὶ ἐν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν αὐτῶν.
hint: These are the sons of Ham.

notes.text: The plural here, where 10:5 had κατὰ γλῶσσαν.

reading: [[these|these, the nearer, what follows]] sons of [[name:Χαμ]] [[in the races|within, inside of, and by means of the races, the tribes, the bodies united by ties of blood and descent, the clans, the tribes by local habitation, the hundreds and counties, the contingents furnished by a tribe, the brigades]] of them [[down|down, downwards, down from, down upon, over, upon]] [[tongues|tongues, tongues as the organ of speech, tongues and languages, mouthpieces of a pipe]] of them [[in the spaces in which a thing is|within, inside of, and by means of the spaces in which a thing is, the places, the positions and posts, the places in life and stations, the lands and countries, the pieces of land and estates and farms, the countries]] of them and [[in the numbers of people accustomed to live together|within, inside of, and by means of the numbers of people accustomed to live together, the companies and bodies of men, the hosts, the swarms and flocks, the nations and peoples, the nations and gentiles, the special classes, the castes and tribes, the sexes]] of them.

greek: Καὶ τῷ Σημ ἐγενήθη καὶ αὐτῷ, πατρὶ πάντων τῶν υἱῶν Εβερ, ἀδελφῷ Ιαφεθ τοῦ μείζονος.
hint: To Shem also, the father of all the sons of Eber.

notes.text: The Hebrew *ʾăḥî yepet haggādôl* can be read *the elder brother of Japheth* or *the brother of Japheth the elder*. The Greek genitive τοῦ μείζονος goes with Ιαφεθ: *brother of Japheth the greater*.
No subject is expressed: *there came to be to Shem also*, as the Hebrew *yullad gam-hûʾ*.

reading: And to [[name:Σημ]] [[came into being|there came to be, there arose, there was brought into existence]] also to him, [[to father|to father, to grandfather]] [[of all|of all, of the whole, of every, of every single]] of the sons of [[name:Εβερ]], [[to son of the same mother|to a son of the same mother, to a brother, to a near kinsman]] of [[name:Ιαφεθ]] [[of the bigger|of the bigger, of the greater, of the taller, of the vaster, of the stronger and mightier, of the weightier and more important]].

names.gloss: (Εβερ, from Hebrew ʿĒber, "the region beyond")

greek: υἱοὶ Σημ· Αιλαμ καὶ Ασσουρ καὶ Αρφαξαδ καὶ Λουδ καὶ Αραμ καὶ Καιναν.
hint: The sons of Shem, with Cainan, whom the Hebrew does not have.

notes.text: [[flag]] Not in the Hebrew, whose sons of Shem are five: Elam, Asshur, Arpachshad, Lud and Aram. Luke 3:36 counts him in the line of Jesus, τοῦ Σαλὰ τοῦ Καϊνὰμ τοῦ Ἀρφαξάδ.

reading: sons of [[name:Σημ]]; [[name:Αιλαμ]] and [[name:Ασσουρ]] and [[name:Αρφαξαδ]] and [[name:Λουδ]] and [[name:Αραμ]] and [[name:Καιναν]].

names.gloss: (Αιλαμ, from Hebrew ʿÊlām, the land east of Babylonia)
(Αρφαξαδ, from Hebrew ʾArpakšad, of uncertain meaning)
(Λουδ, from Hebrew Lûd, of uncertain meaning)
(Αραμ, from Hebrew ʾĂrām, the Arameans)
(Καιναν, a son of Arphaxad whom the Hebrew does not name; the name of 5:9, Hebrew Qênān)

greek: καὶ υἱοὶ Αραμ· Ως καὶ Ουλ καὶ Γαθερ καὶ Μοσοχ.
hint: The sons of Aram.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *Maš*. The Greek repeats Μοσοχ, Meshech, the son of Japheth at 10:2.

reading: and sons of [[name:Αραμ]]; [[name:Ως]] and [[name:Ουλ]] and [[name:Γαθερ]] and [[name:Μοσοχ]].

names.gloss: (Ως, from Hebrew ʿÛṣ, of uncertain meaning)
(Ουλ, from Hebrew Ḥûl, of uncertain meaning)
(Γαθερ, from Hebrew Geter, of uncertain meaning)

greek: καὶ Αρφαξαδ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Καιναν, καὶ Καιναν ἐγέννησεν τὸν Σαλα, Σαλα δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Εβερ.
hint: Arphaxad, Cainan, Shelah, Eber.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *wĕʾarpakšad yālad ʾet-šālaḥ*, *Arpachshad begot Shelah*. The Greek puts Cainan between them, and so does Luke 3:35–36.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus reads Καιναμ, both times: Luke's spelling.

reading: and [[name:Αρφαξαδ]] [[begot|begot, engendered, brought forth, produced]] [[name:Καιναν]], and [[name:Καιναν]] [[begot|begot, engendered, brought forth, produced]] [[name:Σαλα]], [[name:Σαλα]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand]], [[begot|begot, engendered, brought forth, produced]] [[name:Εβερ]].

names.gloss: (Σαλα, from Hebrew Šelaḥ, usually connected with šālaḥ, "to send")

greek: καὶ τῷ Εβερ ἐγενήθησαν δύο υἱοί· ὄνομα τῷ ἑνὶ Φαλεκ, ὅτι ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις αὐτοῦ διεμερίσθη ἡ γῆ, καὶ ὄνομα τῷ ἀδελφῷ αὐτοῦ Ιεκταν.
hint: Peleg, in whose days the earth was divided.

notes.text: The Hebrew plays the name *Peleg* against *niplĕgâ*, *was divided*. The Greek keeps the name and translates the verb, διαμερίζω, *to distribute, to divide*, and the play is gone.

reading: and to [[name:Εβερ]] [[came into being|came to be, arose, were brought into existence]] two sons; [[a name|a name, fame, a mere name, a phrase and expression]] [[to the one|to the one, to a single one, to one alone]] [[name:Φαλεκ]], [[that|that, seeing that, although, for that, because, inasmuch as]] [[in the days|within, inside of, and by means of the days, the day-breaks, the times]] of him [[was distributed|was distributed, was divided]] [[the earth|the land, the dry ground, the terrestrial realm]], and [[a name|a name, fame, a mere name, a phrase and expression]] [[to the son of the same mother|to the son of the same mother, to the brother, to the near kinsman]] of him [[name:Ιεκταν]].

names.gloss: (Φαλεκ, from Hebrew Peleg, "division", which the verse ties to pālag, "to divide")
(Ιεκταν, from Hebrew Yoqṭān, usually connected with qāṭān, "small")

greek: Ιεκταν δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ελμωδαδ καὶ τὸν Σαλεφ καὶ Ασαρμωθ καὶ Ιαραχ
hint: The sons of Joktan.

notes.text: [[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus reads τόν before Ασαρμωθ, and alone reads Ιαραδ.

reading: [[name:Ιεκταν]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand]], [[begot|begot, engendered, brought forth, produced]] [[name:Ελμωδαδ]] and [[name:Σαλεφ]] and [[name:Ασαρμωθ]] and [[name:Ιαραχ]]

(Σαλεφ, from Hebrew Šālep, of uncertain meaning)
(Ασαρμωθ, from Hebrew Ḥăṣarmāwet, "court of death")
(Ιαραχ, from Hebrew Yeraḥ, "moon")

greek: καὶ Οδορρα καὶ Αιζηλ καὶ Δεκλα
hint: Hadoram, Uzal, Diklah.

notes.text: For the Hebrew *Hădôrām*.

reading: and [[name:Οδορρα]] and [[name:Αιζηλ]] and [[name:Δεκλα]]

names.gloss: (Οδορρα, from Hebrew Hădôrām, of uncertain meaning)
(Αιζηλ, from Hebrew ʾÛzāl, of uncertain meaning)
(Δεκλα, from Hebrew Diqlâ, "palm grove")

greek: καὶ Αβιμεηλ καὶ Σαβευ
hint: Abimael and Sheba; the Hebrew's Obal is missing.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew has *ʿÔbāl* before *ʾĂbîmāʾēl*; the Greek does not.

reading: and [[name:Αβιμεηλ]] and [[name:Σαβευ]]

names.gloss: (Αβιμεηλ, from Hebrew ʾĂbîmāʾēl, beginning ʾābî, "my father", and ending ʾēl, "God")
(Σαβευ, from Hebrew Šĕbāʾ, of uncertain meaning)

greek: καὶ Ουφιρ καὶ Ευιλα καὶ Ιωβαβ. πάντες οὗτοι υἱοὶ Ιεκταν.
hint: Ophir, Havilah, Jobab: all the sons of Joktan.

notes.text: The name of 10:7, a second bearer; the Hebrew is *Ḥăwîlâ* both times.

reading: and [[name:Ουφιρ]] and [[name:Ευιλα]] and [[name:Ιωβαβ]]. [[all|all, the whole, every, every single]] [[these|these, the nearer, what follows]] sons of [[name:Ιεκταν]].

names.gloss: (Ουφιρ, from Hebrew ʾÔpîr, of uncertain meaning)
(Ιωβαβ, from Hebrew Yôbāb, of uncertain meaning)

greek: καὶ ἐγένετο ἡ κατοίκησις αὐτῶν ἀπὸ Μασση ἕως ἐλθεῖν εἰς Σωφηρα, ὄρος ἀνατολῶν.
hint: Their dwelling, from Mesha to Sephar, the mountain of the east.

notes.text: κατοίκησις, *a settling in*, one sense, is plain text; the Hebrew *môšābām*, *their dwelling*.
*A mountain of risings*: the Hebrew *har haqqedem*, *the hill country of the east*.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus alone reads Μασσηε.

reading: and [[came into being|came to be, arose, was brought into existence]] the settling in of them [[from|from, away from, far from, apart from]] [[name:Μασση]] [[until|until, till, while, so long as]] [[to come|to come, to go, to go back and return, to be going to and intend, to come within a little of and be near]] [[into|into, to, in, rest in]] [[name:Σωφηρα]], [[a mountain|a mountain, a hill]] [[of risings|of risings, of rises, of the quarter of sunrise, of the east]].

names.gloss: (Μασση, from Hebrew Mēšāʾ, of uncertain meaning)
(Σωφηρα, from Hebrew Sĕpārâ, the name with its ending of direction, "toward Sephar")
